chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al- Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Abdul Samad ibn Muhammad, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), from his father (peace be upon him), who said:

Imamate is not valid except for a man who possesses three characteristics: piety that restrains him from forbidden deeds; patience that enables him to control his anger; and good deputyship over those he leads, so that he is like a merciful father to them.
ai.seo_question: What are the three key characteristics required for a leader in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights these three traits as the foundational criteria for the Imamate, emphasizing that spiritual integrity (war') and emotional mastery (hilm) must be complemented by practical administrative excellence (husn al-khilafah). This triad ensures the leader not only avoids sin but also governs with the nurturing authority of a 'merciful father,' reflecting the Shia ideal of the Imam as both a spiritual guide and a just ruler.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-97 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Abdul Samad ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Han’nan ibn Sadeer, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) that his father (MGB) said,

“No one deserves to be a leader unless he has three characteristics: piety which would hinder him from doing the forbidden deeds; patience which would help him control his anger; and good deputyship over those whom he leads just as if he is their kind father.”
